## Natural history notes

A medium-sized lady beetle characterized by a rounded, glossy body that varies from orange to red or even nearly black, usually with several dark spots and a pale pronotum often marked with a black “M” or “W” shape. In Florida, the Asian Lady Beetle is found in gardens, fields, orchards, forest edges, parks, yards, and around buildings, especially where aphids and other soft-bodied insects are abundant. Both adults and larvae are predators of aphids, scales, and other small plant-feeding insects, but the species is introduced and can become a nuisance when adults gather on or inside buildings during cooler weather.
